speechtext: As my right hon. friend knows, the population of the Yukon is becoming so reduced that the overhead expense of government is enormous. It is in order to cut down the expense that I am asking for this amendment.

maintopic: LAND TITLES ACT-AMENDMENT
speechtext:
All right.
Bill reported, read the third time and passed.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is it the pleasure of the committee that this vote be taken item by item?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Yes.
Apple River-breakwater repairs, $2,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Where is Apple river?

speakeroldname: Hon. J. H. KING (Minister of Public Works):
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: In the county of Cumberland. The money is needed for repairs to the breakwater approach.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I notice the vote is for
repairs. What happened?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
No repairs or
improvements have been made to this breakwater since it was constructed in 1907.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Has it been much used?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It is a farming
and lumbering settlement of about two hundred people. The breakwater is to provide shelter for vessels loading lumber, the shipments amounting to between ten and fifteen million feet a year. Shipments are temporarily held up owing to a recent transfer of the lumber property, but will be resumed in the near future.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Were the fifteen million
feet shipments lately or long ago?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Shipments are
temporarily held up.

Item agreed to.
Babin's cove-wharf extension, $1,700.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is a new wharf?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the total length of
the wharf?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It consists of a
block and span one hundred feet long by twenty feet wide, with an "L" twenty-five feet in width projecting twenty feet from the southern side of the outer channel. In 1910 a warehouse twenty-five feet by sixteen feet was built at the head of the wharf, greatly interfering with the turning space for teams. To widen this turning space is the principal reason for the extension.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What industry is carried on on the island?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: There is a general development carried on. The island has a population of 3,000 people.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Was this shed put up in such a way that the wharf could not be used?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Apparently.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Was it put up by the same engineer w'ho is now recommending how to undo his mistake?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I am not sure.

Item agreed to.
Bass River-improvements, $1,500.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Where is Bass River?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Colchester county.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What are the improvements to consist of?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: It is to construct a crib protection work for a vessel bed, to be built in two sections; also minor repairs. The vessels go up on the tide and rest on the mud when the tide recedes, and this bed is to hold the vessel on an even keel when the tide is out.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Will this list take care of all the improvements necessary in the way of harbours and wharves in Nova Scotia? That is, shall we have no further items in the supplementary estimates?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: It is pretty hard to say.

Item agreed to.
Bayfield-breakwater repairs, $6,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is a reconstruction of both sides of breakwater for a distance of 420 feet, the work to be effected by setting stone in concrete.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: When did the destruction take place?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
In the storm of
October 1, 1923.

Item agreed to.
Bay St. Lawrence-'breakwater repairs, $5,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: That is in Cape Breton North.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What has happened here?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The damage was caused by a storm on October 2nd, 1923. The Department of Marine and Fisheries strongly urged that this breakwater be repaired.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What is the report from that department?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I have only a reference to a letter written on October 17, 1923, by the Department of Marine and Fisheries strongly urging that these repairs be made. I have not the letter here.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What was the
date of the by-election there?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: In August, I think -before the storm anyway.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Of what is this breakwater
constructed?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Of native timber crib work filled with stone.

Item agreed to.
Broad Cove marsh-replacement breakwater wharf, $8,400.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What county is this in?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Inverness.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Why was the
work not done last year? Is this because of an anticipated storm that did cot arise?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: They had difficulty in getting the labour last fall and the contract was let in March of this year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: For what price?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: $7,329. The contractor is with the Sydney Construction Company.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: There were hundreds of people out of work; why could not the labour be secured?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I have not the
details as to that.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Perhaps the member for the riding will give us the real reason.
Supply-Harbours and Rivers

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The explanation is
simple. It is difficult to get the timber there at that time of the year, and that was really the cause of the delay. Labour was very plentiful down there; we were well employed in that part of the country last year. It is a rather rough country and you need the snow in the winter to get the timber out. The timber is there now and the structure is about completed.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Has the timber that has been brought there been paid for?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Not yet.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Has the government considered the advisability of making a permanent construction by pouring cement around the rocks in the cribwork?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I hardly think so.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: You will find that concrete construction in every stream and every river in this country where abutments are put in to protect bridges from the action of ice.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: That is solid concrete but to pour concrete around the boulders in the crib would not be effective. Moreover, it would not be satisfactory in salt water.

Item agreed to.
Cariboo Island-breakwater reconstruction, $8,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Was this carried away too?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
This is in the
county of Pictou, N.S.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is this let by contract?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: It will be.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: There is $2,000 already spent on it. What happened?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Certain work was being carried on last year with the vote, following a storm which destroyed not only some of the work that had been done but another section of the breakwater as well. It had originally been intended to do this work by contract, but when the storm occurred we used a certain amount of money to hold what we had remaining of the breakwater.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: There were no tenders called for, then?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
We were calling for tenders last season when the storm occurred, destroying another section of the breakwater, and it was considered inadvisable CMr M^iab*** '
to let a contract that season. The engineer was instructed to expend a certain sum of money to ensure the safety of what was left, with a view to asking parliament for a revote to carry on the reconstruction this season.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Why could the tender
not be gone on with notwithstanding the storm? Is the minister going on with tenders now?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: We will complete the work by day's labour now.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Why?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Because we think it is in the interests of the department to do so. We started to do certain work last fall, and we will continue the work by day's labour, as it is more economical.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Why was it more economical to do it by tender before the storm and more economical to do it by day labour after the storm? Did the storm upset the whole principle of the department?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Oh no, but the situation was changed very much after the storm, and we then decided to carry on by day labour to retain, if possible, what was remaining. It is considered by the department that we had better continue as we have begun, under the direction of the engineers.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is the work being done on a percentage basis?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: No, the department is doing it.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Was this the October
storm too?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

Item agreed to.
Carr's Brook-breakwater repairs, $1,275.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is that the same storm?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
No. This is to
renew the stringers where necessary. There was a storm in that vicinity that disturbed the structure somewhat, and this vote is for repairs.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What storm was that?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: On October 1st and 2nd.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Where is Carr's Brook?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
In Colchester
county.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What river is the breakwater in? Is it out in the ocean?

Supply-Harbours and Rivers

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Carr's Brook
enters into Minas Basin. The wharf is at the mouth of the river, I suppose on Carr's Brook, at Minas Basin.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is this by tender too?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
No, by day
labour.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Has anything been done by tender of all the list so far?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Yes, the larger
item for Broad Cove marsh. Tenders were called for that work.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Did the storm not change the minister's idea there?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: No.

Item agreed to.
Chimney Comer-wharf reconstruction, $8,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Just why is the minister
spending $8,000 on a very unimportant place of this kind? Is there any coal business or any business of any kind being done there? Is there any population there? This is the same thing as last year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is for the reconstruction of a wharf destroyed by a storm last October. The industries are farming, fishing, and coal mining.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: That storm must have been a cyclone.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: A storm on the Atlantic covers the whole coast pretty well. A storm in the vicinity of North Cape Breton, for instance, or on the north or south coast of Nova Scotia is not confined to one harbour, but covers the coast pretty generally.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is not on the Atlantic mast at all. The storm could not have hit .here too.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is a very important .ittle harbour. My hon. friend seems to be impressed with the idea that there is nothing going on there. I do not know for a certainty where he got his information, but I think he gets it from someone pretty close to himself.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I know something about this particular section. I do not have to ask my hon. friend to my left (Mr. Black, Halifax).

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
There are four fishing establishments there carrying on business through all the open season of the year. There is also a coal mine which is going to be operated just as soon as it is possible to carry the coal away from there, but fishing is the im-243
portant thing. If my hon. friend will come down to my part of the country I will take him there, and I am sure he will enjoy himself. It is a magnificent spot.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What was spent there last year, the year before, and the year before that?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Last year's storm destroyed the whole structure, which was in first-class shape till then.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
We have been spending money there right along.
Mr.CHISHOLM: No, this is the third time.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I think we did some work there in 1922, and again in 1923.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
There is a coal prospect there. I wonder if my hon. friend could tell us who control the coal prospect, and whether they have been able to sell it
yet?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I have not any information on that.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I think if my hon. friend will find out who wants this he will be able to get the information.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I have no information.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
No mystery
about it?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I know of none.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: No coal taken out of it yet at all?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
A very considerable
amount of coal has been taken out of it. I may tell my hon. friend that the property is owned by an incorporated company. If he wants further particulars I can tell him that I am a small owner there.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It is just the
facts I want.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Well, the property is
owned by an incorporated company and I am ,i shareholder.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Who are the
ethers?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It is not necessary for
me to give my hon. friend that information is it?



Supply-Harbours and Rivers

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Not if it is withheld.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is there any reason why the hon. member should give his name and not the others?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I might tell my right
hon. friend I thought the ex-Minister of Finance was insinuating something, and that he had me in mind. I have no hesitation in saying that I am a part owner, and that I hope to see the property developed on such a scale that it will be a great benefit to the surrounding country. I have put my own money in this proposition with the hope that I would do something by way of developing that natural resource. Does the hon. member find fault with that?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I think it will
be a good thing.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I wish to tell my hon.
friend that it is not the coal development alone that is looked for a't that particular point; good results have accrued to the fishing industry from the construction of the pier there. There are two fishing establishments in vigorous operation now. A very considerable amount of fishing is done in the neighbourhood, and a considerable amount of business has been transacted as a result of the construction of this wharf. The benefit of the expenditure for this purpose is not confined to this particular community, because that part of the coast is far away from any harbours and boats come here for shelter from other sections.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I may be quite wrong but my recollection is that when the present Judge McKenzie was a member of the House he wanted this work undertaken in connection with the coal development which we would all like to see. I think the work was started in 1922. I cannot believe that this coal development is not going on simply for the lack of an expenditure of $8,000. What is the real reason why this coal development, which was expected to take place in 1922, has not come about?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The reason is very clear. There are no railways to that part of the country and just as soon as this wharf is in shape to take care of the export of coal the coal development will take place. The reason no coal is shipped from there now is that the wharf is not in shape to handle it. A very considerable amount of coal was shipped from there one season, three years ago; but the accommodation was not good enough to enable 
the coal owners to ship anything like substantial quantities from that pier so the operations had to be suspended.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The minister says there was $1,000 spent in 1922-23. The vote in 3922-23 was $18,000. The vote for 1923-24 was $13,400. The latter was said to be a revote so that there must have been $.5,100 spent in the previous year; $11,000 last year, and now $8,000 is asked. What is this coal mine worth?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
An order in
council was passed on August 2, 1922 accepting the tender of W. E. Laundry for $12,159 for the construction of this extension. It was under the estimated cost. My notes show that the expenditure in 1922-23 was $1,100. It was late in the season when the contract was let, and I expect that very little work was done until 1923-24.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
There must have been
$5,100 spent.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: No, I think not.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The $13,400 was a revote the next year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The tender was
very much lower than our original estimate.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Has any coal been shipped out of there?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I have already told my right hon. friend that considerable coal was shipped from there in 1921. I am not able to give him the exact quantity, but I may tell him in order to really carry on a coal business there it is necessary to have a considerable depth of water. The structure at that time would only furnish sufficient depth for small schooners. It was found in the fall of the year, it being a rough coast, that it was necessary to stop shipping because it was difficult to get a schooner of any size to the pier and large vessels were required for the fall trade. That is why this extension was made. The extension was built last year but it was carried away by a storm in October. It is impossible to carry on a coal business there until this work is finished. Again I want to emphasize that it was not for the coal business alone that this pier was originally constructed, It was for the purpose of providing a harbour of shelter for the fishermen along the coast, and they have taken advantage of it to a very considerable extent.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
There has been no coal
shipped since 1921?

Supply-Harbours and Rivers

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Since 1922, to be accurate. I have given the reason why more coal was not shipped.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: When was the pier constructed first?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The first part of it was built in 1921. The coal was shipped in the season following the building of the pier. I might tell my hon. friend that a considerable amount of money was spent there developing that coal property, the expectation being that there would be a sufficient depth of water to permit the shipment of larger quantities.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I think my hon. friend must be wrong in his dates?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I may be mistaken as to the exact date.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Because according to his first statement the shipment was made before the pier was built.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I may be wrong in the date of the construction of the pier, but the shipment took place the year after the pier was built and would have continued if this structure had been sufficiently long to give water enough to enable larger ships to tie to pier. Shipments will start again just as soon as the work is finished.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I point out to the committee that the expenditure for development at Chimney Corner will benefit Prince Edward Island and not merely that part of Cape Breton. It is the nearest point to Prince Edward Island that contains any coal, and many cargoes of coal were shipped from Chimney Corner to Charlottetown and Summerside. It was good coal. It came from the nearest point to us and the freight was very reasonable; we got it at a much cheaper rate than we could get it by rail from other points. I may say that the great majority of our people now use coal for domestic purposes, very largely on account of the scarcity of wood, and they would like to see the coal mine in question developed in order to obtain cheap fuel. The expenditure at Chimney Corner will benefit not only the people of the immediate locality but also the people in other parts of the Maritime provinces and especially those along the coast who are dependent on coal for fuel.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Would my hon. friend tell me the name of the company?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I do not know the name of the company. I can tell my hon. friend that the coal at Chimney Corner is of 243i
very fine quality especially suited for 10 p.m. kitchen use, and it is popular among those in the province of Prince Edward Island who have had the opportunity of using it.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: In what year was this coal shipment made?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The same year it was shipped from Chimney Corner.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What year was that?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I understand it was in 1921 or 1922.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Does the minister say it was the late government that started this work?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Construction was started in 1919-1920.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: There was no vote in 1922.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Yes a contract
was let to Messrs. Morrison, Congdon and Company.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It must have changed
its name.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
No. The wharf
was originally 170 feet long by 20 feet wide. This new section was an extension of a former work started in 1919-20.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: But all this new construction is for the purposes of coal shipments. The place was all right for fish before. There is none of that in the vote under Chimney Comer for 1921-22.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: No; the contract was let for 1919-20, and I suppose it was completed in that period.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Yes and no harm was
ever done to that wharf. That was sufficient for the purposes of the fishing industry.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It was necessary to extend it because there was not sufficient space for the boats. It was the initial step in the contemplated plan. The late government started to build it, and I think if the minister will look over his records, he will see that the first item was only a part of the plan at that time. So much was available for that year and the original plan was to be finished the next year. The first original structure would' certainly not give enough protection to the boats. Two large fishing buildings were put up there for the purpose of buying and exporting fish. The business

Supply-Harbours and Rivers
enlarged and it justified the extension. It was necessary also to give protection to the additional number of boats that came {here as a result of the development that took place.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What portion was destroyed by this storm-the new part or the old?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The new part.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
This seems to have caused a good deal of commotion amongst the people in that vicinity. As I understand the matter, a petition was sent in some time ago, and I have what I think is a copy of it. The residents of St. Rose, who seem to think their place is the one which should be favoured with a wharf, sent this petition to the minister:
We the undersigned citizens do petition asking for consideration for a wharf to be constructed at Saint Rose cove, Inverness county, Cape Breton, Nova Scotia, Canada, as already on petitions for two consecutive years to our member of parliament, Dr. A. W. Chisholm, (for nineteen years representing the county) and to Minister of Public Works, asking for a "wharf" to enable our fishermen a place to land their fish, and a place of protection for their boats, and to have a place to ship material. Recently orders of lumber had had to be cancelled, owing to the fact that we had no place to ship via water, railroad, nor any making. It is very hard for us espcially during the present crisis of hard times, when lumber is the only means we have to earn money to support ourselves and families.
This is signed by all the representative people who live in the place. There are excellent names signed to this petition. There are a large number of 'MacLeods, McRaes, McKenzies, McKinnons, McPhersons. It would be almost like the landing of the Hector to put this on Hansard, so I will forego. I have no doubt that they are excellent citizens. I am favouved with a communication on this subject. I am not responsible for it, but the person seems to be acquainted with certain facts. He says:
For over fifty years money has been spent at Chimney Corner, Inverness county, Cape Breton. Dr. A. W. Chisholm, M.P. for Inverness county has secured $17,000 for a breakwater wharf, and it was built in 1923. The following fall it was destroyed by the fall gales. He had a returned man, Dan McKay, appointed inspector of the wharf works while under construction at $3.50 per day. McKay was at the same time working on the highway with a pair of horses at $6 per day. If he was attending to his job as inspector of the wharf, as freely said, it might be that the wharf would have a different story, than a wreck. Not satisfied with this, McKay was appointed once again by Dr. Chisholm to do the repair work of the old wharf, $800 which was destroyed and six beautiful boats, and lumber on the wharf. Seems strange McKay should be having about all while others get nothing. Dr. Chisholm is interested in the Chimney Corner coal mines, associated with three other colleagues-

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Does it give their
names?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I do not know. I am just reading through.
-but I am told that owing to water trouble, it cannot be a success yet he gets all this money for the place. We cannot leave any material on the wharf. The beach with a brook running through is bad and not much hauling can be done, especially up a steep hill, with millions of cliff stones hanging above and during half a century all this money is spent there. We have been trying to get a wharf constructed as stated on petition, and do not seem to get in fact anything through Dr. Chisholm, yet he can get money for Chimney Corner. Many other efforts have been tried, but nothing doing for this district. Four contracts for lumber had to be cancelled this winter owing to no shipping place for St. Rose. For years we have been trying to get a wharf, and petitioned for it every year. Last year we do not think Dr. Chisholm introduced the bill.
Of course, we know that this does not come in by a bill unless it is for the services of a wharf inspector.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the name of the
last writer?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: It was written by Mr. A. J. MacLeod who, I believe, is a near relative of the representative of the country.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
That is the reason for it,
I suppose.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I am informed:
That these people have already petitioned twice through the representative of this county to have this expenditure made. They claim Dr. Chisholm has ignored them and instead of trying to get a vote for a wharf at St. Rose bent his energies to get money spent at Chimney Comer where the doctor has coal mining interests. The people of this St. Rose district-
I am sure the other side of the House will be glad to hear this.
-were very strong in the Liberal political faith. At the last federal election, I got only 24 votes in this district and the total vote ,polled was over 200.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Twenty-four too many.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Too many from the
Liberal point of view. The hon. member had better do something, for he cannot expect people to vote for their representative unless they get a vote for a wharf.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I will take my chances.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The hon. member had
better remember Tim and the success of the breakwater. There ought at least to be a wharf of a reasonable size built there:
The majority of the men whose names appear on their petition were strong supporters of Dr. A. W. Chisholm at the last election. They are much opposed to him now on account of this matter.
Think of the chances he is willing to take! Apparently there is no change in their political

Supply-Harbours and Rivers
faith, but there is some dissatisfaction at the lack of activity of the representative of their constituency. It seems to me only fair to give an opportunity to the hon. member for Inverness to explain how soon he will have a wharf built at St. Rose, and why he persists in favouring Chimney Corner at the expense of St. Rose, which, from the petition and the correspondence I have read, appears to be indisputably entitled to a wharf. It is a place where a wharf will stand, where a wharf will not fall out like the one at Chimney Corner. It will be a public utility. The hon. member should give some apology to his constituents to-night and show some signs of repentance.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I am glad my hon. friend has brought this matter up. The fact of the matter is that I have put forth all the efforts in me for four consecutive years in trying to get a wharf built at St. Rose. Reports were made by the engineers setting forth that it was an impossibility to construct a wharf there at any reasonable cost. It is a fact also that the late government made a report in regard to the matter. If they failed to get the wharf, that was not on account of any lack of persistence on my part, because I endeavoured to get the department to see as I saw. I would like very well to have a wharf at St. Rose myself if it could be built at a reasonable cost.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
How did you succeed in
Chimney Corner?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I succeeded there because nature helped me, and because the wharf would be a great benefit when it was put there. So far as St. Rose is concerned, it is in my own neighbourhood, and I am very grateful to my hon. friend for his interest in it. I know MacLeod is a relative of mine. My hon. friend will find it one of the most difficult things in the world to satisfy some of his relatives sometimes. So far as his criticism of Mr. McKay is concerned, my hon. friend should be ashamed to read a letter like that, couched in poor English and worse judgment. He was the only returned soldier there. He left home in 1914 and remained overseas until 1918. But let me ask my hon. friend if he knows whether MacLeod went overseas or not. That gentleman took very great care that he remained on his father's farm, when he was just as well able to go. when McKay went. He seems terribly distressed because I recognized this soldier who has sacrificed so much for his country. Mr. McKay is possessed of a substantial amount of intelligence. I cannot say that much for Mr. MacLeod as is clearly shown
by his letter. So far as the district of St. Rose is concerned, I may tell my hon. friend that I got eveiy vote in that district, twelve miles distant, except Mr. MacLeod's vote.
I suppose that may explain why he is so persistent in writing childish letters.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: He was not a warrior.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
He certainly was not a warrior in that case, and I do not think his sympathies were strongly in that direction. I will be very glad if my hon. friend will help me to get a wharf at St. Rose. If he goes with me to the department we will try to satisfy the department that there is a justification for the expenditure. We have failed so far. It is impossible to convince the engineer that a wharf should be placed there.
I do not know that I can give my hon. friend any more explanation than that, but I am sure he should be satisfied with it inasmuch as his own party when in power never spent a dollar in any part of that district.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The information is very
nice indeed, and the hon. member has his chance now. If he will induce the minister to put a decent little sum in the estimates to put a wharf at St. Rose, I think I can guarantee the support of all the members of this group, and I think I can go him one better. If he will cease accumulating votes in those districts in the way he has been doing in the past, and give us a chance to take over the reins of government ourselves, we will put a wharf there, and we will not find that nature will interfere with it. We will employ returned soldiers in connection with it, but not returned soldiers holding two incompatible jobs at the same time.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: That statement is not correct. This man who writes the letter exaggerates. Mr. McKay is a responsible man who would not be guilty of such a thing. He is a leading citizen of that community and he would be the last man who would try to fill two positions at the same time. Mr. MacLeod has not been telling the truth. So far as my hon. friend's graciousness goes, his party was in power previously, and the county of Inverness sent a representative supporting the party. I think there was one pier built in Inverness county during that long eighteen years. His party was also in power from 1911 to 1917.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Longer than that.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I would advise my hon.
friend not to worry. If the wharf should not be built there, surely he does not think he could induce the Minister of Public Works to put it in the supplementary estimates.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I did not say I could.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
My proposition is that if
the minister would put an item in the supplementary .estimates we would vote for it.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It has been stated either
by the minister or my hon. friend on the other side of the House that this coal mine would not pay unless we had boats of large dimensions coming in. I presume this is an endeavour to insert the thin end of the wedge, and next time we will have to spend ten or fifteen thousand dollara in dredging, to allow the larger boats to come in.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I do not think there was a range of a hundred yards along the whole Atlantic coast where the government did not provide last year to build a wharf. I remember it well. It was the same thing this year. It seems to me there is not a quarter of a mile along the coast where the government is not providing for a wharf. What is the object? To keep them in power all the time?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Is it. a fact that the
principal stockholders in this coal company are members of this House and members of the Senate of Canada?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I have no information to that effect. I have no knowledge of it.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Perhaps the hon. member for Inverness might tell us.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Would my hon. friend
expect me to give him all the information with respect to my private business or anything else? Would he like me to ask him a similar question? He can find out if he is anxious to do so. It is known as the Chimney Corner Coal Company.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: It is understood in some sections that the colleagues of my hon. friend own the stock in this company, and that they are endeavouring to have public money spent to build a wharf with a view of having large improvements. I understand they want the money spent to build a wharf, in order that they may sell the property.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I may satisfy my hon.
.friend by telling him that they have no intention of selling the property. It is not for sale, and my hon. friend's informants should get a little better acquainted with the circumstances of the company. They are not trying to sell.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I am trying to get information.

Item agreed to.
Comeau's Cove-breakwater improvement, $-1,900.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What happened at Comeau's Cove?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
This item is to
build a new cribwork block on the harbour side of the breakwater and a native timber, stone-filled crib. It is to protect the local fishing fleet. The existing work consists of a breakwater built in 1914-15. I think that covers the structure to date.

Item agreed to.
Digby-repairs and renewals to pier, [DOT] $2,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is to be
done this year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Renewals of floors, fenders and freight shed repairs. It is annual repair work necessary on account of great and constant wear and tear.

Item agreed to.	-
Dartmouth

pier, $120,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
This is a large item. What is the present position?

Supply-Harbours and Rivers

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
This is for the
construction of a pier 661 feet long, consisting of stone with gravel approaches. The work is under contract to the Halifax Dredging Company and the Standard Construction Company. The amount of the contract is $135,659.54. The probable expenditure for 1923-24 is $25,000. There is a re-vote of $50,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Then the other
figure must be wrong.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
That was the
probable expenditure when the estimates were being made up. The actual expenditure was $22,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: How can that be in view of these figures?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: You have inspection fees as well, and then expenditure for the site, $6,802.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Is the vote of
$120,000 going to clean up the whole matter?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I hope this is
not a place where the wharf is going to be carried away by storms.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Halifax is a protected harbour.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
No trouble up
there at all?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I think not.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Is this entirely
new work?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What constituency?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Halifax.

Item agreed to.
East Bay-wharf repairs, $1,600.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Any storms
there?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
No; this is a
renewal of stringers, guard rail covering, and so forth, which are in a decayed condition.

Item agreed to.
East River-repairs to lock, $3,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the
occasion for that work?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
To repair the
lock walls, which the district engineer states are badly disintegrating and may fall into the lock and block navigation.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The $4,000 spent last year was to do similar work. What has happened in the meantime?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The repairs were
not completed last year. This work is of concrete, there has been a very considerable disintegration, and the engineer recommends that if the work is to be saved these repairs must be made.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
How much
money was spent last year?
Mr. KING Kootenay: We spent $4,096.35.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Then I point out to my hon. friendl that the whole of the money that was to be sufficient to repair this work last year has been spent. Now, what has happened?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is additional work.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I know; but
w'hat has happened to bring about this very bad state of affairs when $4,000 was to put the work in proper condition last year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is additional work required this year. The undertaking cost nearly $400,000, and a repair of $4,000 would not be very great.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Will the same
thing be required next year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I cannot say.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I should think
the minister can say if he has the engineer's report before him.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
No, that could
not be reported at this time. The report from the district engineer covers the requirement for this year. By next November or December we will probably be getting a further report on this work. It is a large work.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Of course it
is a large work. It must follow that the minister should know whether further repairs are under contemplation or not. Last year $4,000 was not enough to look after the necessary repairs, although, so far as my memory goes, it was considered sufficient. There has been no storm to interfere with the lock since. The whole trouble we are told was that the work was large and the engineer did not completely cover the repairs. Now I ask the minister does this $3,000 cover it, or is he coming back next year for another $3,000 or $4,000?

Supply-Harbours and Rivers

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I am asking parliament to vote what the engineer considers necessary to take care of the repairs this year. The work is of concrete. This concrete is disintegrating, and when disintegration sets in in concrete it is difficult to say what repairs will be necessary year by year. My hon. friend is well versed in that.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Does this sum cover all the repairs necessary to look after the concrete that has disintegrated?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It is what the
engineer has asked for this year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I am asking,
Mr. Chairman, whether this sum will cover all repairs for concrete that is disintegrating.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: No one can tell you that at the present time.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Has any disintegration evidenced itself that it is not now intended to repair?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I have not had a report on that.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What does the report say?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I read the report: This amount of $3,000 is required to repair the lock walls, which the district engineer states are badly disintegrating, and may fall in the lock and block navigation if not repaired. That is the district engineer's reason for the expenditure. As to further disintegration, I have not any report, and it is impossible to say that this will be the only amount required for years to come.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I am asking if this sum is sufficient to cover the repairs for this year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: We will probably have a report on this work at the end of the season suggesting the requirements for next year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Where has this happened?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: It is a lock between Pictou and New Glasgow. Two ferries operate daily between these towns, and a large number of boats use the channel. This lock was built as part of a general river improvement project carried out from 1908 to 1918. A contract was let for this work in 1913.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What is the cause of the disintegration-bad work in the beginning?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It is the effect of salt water.
fSir Henry Drayton.]

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I did not know salt water would have that effect.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes, it has a very serious effect on concrete.

Item agreed to.
Eastern Harbour-improvements, $42,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Do we derive any real
benefit from the expenditure of this money? How is it that $38,000 was voted last year and now we have an item of $42,000?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The contract was entered into last year late in the season, .but it was difficult to get tenders at that time and very little was done; about $6,000 or $7,000 was expended. This is to continue the contract.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: To whom has the contract been awarded?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
New Glasgow
Dredging Company.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: In what county is Eastern Harbour situated?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Inverness.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Will this vote
complete the work?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the nature of the
improvements?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Dredging a channel into the harbour.

Item agreed to.
French Village-rebuilding wharf, $3,700.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Where is French Village?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: In the constituency of Halifax. The vote is to rebuild the pile work of a portion of the wharf, 150 by 25 feet. The district engineer on January, 12, 1924, says that the proposed work is of an urgent nature. The wharf is the only one in that vicinity and is used by the residents to land freight brought by vessels from Halifax, also for the export of fish, cordwood, lumber, and so on.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Is there any
revenue from this wharf?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: No.

Item agreed to.
Friar's Head-harbour improvements, $1,500,

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the
nature of the work there?

Supply-Harbours and Rivers

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
$500 to complete
payment on contract for the extension of breakwater; $1,000 for the removal of large boulders and ledge rock a't the approach to the harbour.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What was the
$4,200 spent for last year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The contract last year was for the raising of 105 feet of the breakwater to a further height of 3 feet and the construction of a new section 60 feet in length.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Will this complete the work?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I think so.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: There is nothing more asked for?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Not at present.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Where is Friar's Head?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
In the county of
Inverness.

Item agreed to.
Great Village-wharf replacement, $3,500.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Will the minister explain the nature of this work?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
This work is in
the constituency of Colchester. It is to construct a wharf to replace the old structure, which was in a dilapidated condition and was entirely wrecked by a severe storm in October, 1923.

Item agreed to.
Grand Narrows-wharf extension, $2,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: How was it we did no work there last year? Is there the same lack of necessity now that there was in 1923-24 as evidenced by the action of the department?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The engineer
states that there was difficulty in getting delivery of creosoted timber; that the cost was excessive and he was convinced that a postponement of the expenditure for one year would be advisable.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What was
his estimate of the cost?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What was the
price he indicated as excessive?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: He did not state the amount; he simply said that the price was excessive and that he considered it inadvisable to proceed with the work.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the
present information?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
He says that
since last summer a new view of the creosote situation has arisen. The plans of Creosote Products Limited of Toronto indicate that they will establish creosote works at Newcastle, New Brunswick, and New Glasgow, Nova Scotia, and the probability is they will be able to supply all the creosoted materials required for these and other works at much more reasonable figures than those received during the past year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Where is Grand Narrows?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Cape Breton
North and Victoria.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Is this work
done by tender and contract?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I think it is done by day labour.

Item agreed to.
Harbours and rivers generally-repairs and improvements, $55,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: How much was spent last year under that vote?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Was that work done by tender or by day labour?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Mostly by day
labour. The amounts are small, varying from $30 to $1,400.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: That is to take care of unforeseen expenditures in the way of repairs and so on?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is there any report covering the various items, or is it just a lump sum put in to take care of repairs that crop up from time to time?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
A sum put in
to take care of repairs that become necessary from time to time.
Item agreed to.

Supply-Harbours and Rivers
Irish Cove-wharf repairs, $3,500.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What has happened in Irish Cove?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: We are replacing the native timber piling in the wharf there with creosoted timber. The native timber has been' badly eaten by teredo and the early destruction of the wharf would be inevitable if this piling was not replaced with creosoted timber.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: When was that wharf put in?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: In 1920 the piling was put in.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
So that a
wharf that was put in in 1920 is already so far gone that we have to put in new timber?
Mr. KING (Kootenay: That might easily happen if we have the teredo in that vicinity. The native timber which has not been treated may not last a year under those conditions.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: In what county is Irish Cove?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Cape Breton
South.
Little Bass River-repairs to channel protection work,

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Where is that?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
In Colchester
county.
Lunenburg-dredging, $51,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Where is Lunenburg?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: In the constituency of Lunenburg. It is an important fishing harbour.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Does this dredging have to
be done annually? I see there was a vote for $40,000 last year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The Acadia Contractors Limited.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Have they got the contract also for this further expenditure?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is to complete their contract.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: But is that quite right? The whole vote last year, for $40,000, has been spent apparently. What authority had the government to enter into a contract for more then the $40,000 voted last year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The amount of
the contract was $81,840.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I would like to find out definitely what the practice of the department is. It may be there is some use in considering estimates; it may be there is none at all; it may be the minister is entirely a law unto himself. But here is a vote for $40,000, which so far as I know, and so far as is shown in the estimates, is the sole justification for entering into a contract. Now we are told that a contract has been entered into, not for $40,000, but for $81,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: It is not unusual to vote a sum for a contract, and then to increase the contract and come to parliament next year for an additional amount to complete. The advantage in letting the larger contract would be the opportunity of getting a lower price than if a smaller quantity was moved. The contract price is considered fair and reasonable by the department, and we are asking for this vote to complete the contract.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Surely the minister can see the result of it all. Last year there was doubtless the usual discussion as to the necessity for dredging at this point, and we were doubtless told that dredging should be done to the extent of $40,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
There has not
been any dredging done there for some years, and there is a considerable amount of it to be done.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I think the whole contract was discussed last year. I have the information here, but cannot find it at the moment.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
There was some done last
year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: By contract or day labour?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: By contract.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Who had the contract last
year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I would be interested to know if that was the fact.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The minister last year stated that the estimated cost of dredging would be $103,000, and that the work would be done by tender, so the House was advised at that time that the expenditure would be larger than the vote then asked.

Supply-Harbours and Rivers

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is this to complete the balance of the dredging at the harbour?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is to complete the contract.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is it contemplated there will be further dredging necessary there?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: We hope so; it needs it.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I am not in a
position to say, but there are requests from the engineering department for further dredging at Lunenburg.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Is the dredging
being done for greater area or greater depth?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It is to provide
an area where the ships may lie during the winter season when they return from the banks and crowd into the harbour. At the present time there is not sufficient mooring space for the ships when they come home.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Then it is for
extra space?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Dredging the channel and around the piers.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What depth is
the channel being dredged?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Eighteen feet.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
That is, the
channel to the pier?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Are we troubled with silting there?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Yes, there is
some silt from the sea wash.

Item agreed to.
Malagash-dredging, $22,700.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What about this
case?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This work is necessary in order to permit steamers to enter into the harbour to receive cargoes of salt. Important salt discoveries have been made at this point, and by opening up the channel steamers will be able to come in and receive cargoes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Where is this?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
In Cumberland
county.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What did we spend last year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Practically nothing.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the
reason for the change? Why did we not go on last year and why are we going on this year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The contract was entered into last fall, and it was impossible to get the plant then.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: To whom has the contract been let, and for what amount?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It was let on
October 4, 1923, to the Fraser Paving and Construction Company Limited for the dredging of approximately 23,920 cubic yards, at $2.35 for class A material, and 90 cents for class B.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What does that mean?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Class A is rock, and class B is gravel, sand, clay and other material.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is the work being undertaken this year greater in extent than was proposed last year? The contract last year was only for $15,700.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: We are asking for $22,700 this year, of which $15,700 is a revote. We know better now what the cost will be. We have had tenders since we asked for the vote last year, and the lowest tender was for $22,000 odd.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
But it is for
exactly the same work?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

Item agreed to.
McKay's Point-wharf repairs, $2,700.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is new.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
This is for the
construction of the outer part of this wharf and to put in about twenty new stringers. It is not new work, it is reconstruction.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Where is Mc-
Kay's Point?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
In Cape Breton
North and Victoria.
Item agreed to .
Merigomish-wharf repairs, $1,400.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Where is this?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
In Pictou county. Item agreed to.

Supply-Harbours and Rivers
Meteghan-wharf extension, $6,500.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the
object of this extension?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is in Yarmouth and Clare.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is entirely a revote. Has the contract been let?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Tenders were received and the order in council was passed in September, 1923, for this work.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What was the
amount of the contract?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The contract
was for $5,673.

Item agreed to.
New Harris-wharf, $8,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: How much was spent last year on that?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: We did not expend any money there.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the
reason for the increase from $5,000 to
$8,000?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The engineer increased his estimate by $3,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Yes, but what
was the reason of the increase? Is he committing us to more work, or was his first estimate hopelessly out?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The other
estimate evidently was too low.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What is his explanation; what does he say in his report?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Last year apparently he found cresosoted timber very high and had his estimates too low. He figures this year that his creosoted timber, 10,300 cubic feet, will cost $4,120. Then he is using more native timber which he estimates will cost $2,400. And there is the purchase of right of way, filling, and contingencies, making a total of $8,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Is the precaution taken to
see that all native timber is creosoted in a proper manner before it is put in?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: We are using creosoted timber a great deal more than formerly.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is it the practice to creosote all native timber?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
We use some
native timber.
[Mr. J. H. King.)

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Without creosoting it?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
There is $2,400
worth in this item for example?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It seems to me that since
experience has shown that timber deteriorates very rapidly, sometimes in the space of two or three years, the precaution should be taken to see that all timber placed in wharves, and similar structures, is creosoted.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The creosoted
timber is used more under water, whereas the native timber is used above and on the inside of the work.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Is this new
work?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the
purpose of it?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
To enable the
subsidized steamer which passes daily during the season to call for freight, passengers and so forth. The district contains a scattered farming population. The nearest public wharf at present is at New Campbellton, six miles distant.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What county is
it in?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Cape Breton
North and Victoria.

Item agreed to.
North Ingonish (.McLeod's)-reconstruction of breakwater and dredging, $34,700.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: There has been nothing at all done here has there?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
