Perhaps the
minister will tell us what happened to this matter since he got the vote of $34,700 last year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The delay is due to the lateness of the season when the contract was let. There was no work undertaken there in 1923-24.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
To whom was
the contract let?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
To Thomas D.
Morrison.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the
amount?

Supply-Harbours and Rivers

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The amount is

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Why is the
vote as large as it is?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: There is dredging to be done in addition to the wharf.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Then the
$21,572 is just for the wharf?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the
estimate for dredging?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: To what depth will the dredging be carried and what will be the width?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
There will be
10,500 cubic yards of stone and gravel and also 5,000 of sand and boulders to be dredged inside the breakwater. I do not have the depth in my notes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Would the minister say in what riding this work is?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Cape Breton
North and Victoria.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
About what time were
tenders called for this work last year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The order in
council was passed in November, 1923.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Calling for tenders?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
No, awarding
tenders. Tenders would be called probably in October.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
This is a revote of last
year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Is there any valid reason
why the tenders were not called earlier?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The supply came rather late in the department. This is one of the many works that were up for consideration and plans had to be prepared. I imagine the work was expedited as rapidly as possible.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Why does the
minister say supply was late last year? Supply was voted by the 1st July.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It will be late
this year for public works.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It was passed
before this last year, was it not?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Supply is always
voted late for public works, much to the detriment of the activities of the department. Work cannot be advanced until supply is granted. The result is that many of these works are not undertaken and contracts not awarded until the following spring. That is why many of the works go over until the spring of the following year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Supplies must evidently
have been called in the past for North Ingonish on the same day as for 'Lunenburg.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The department had their supplies presented sufficiently early last year to spend $40,000 in Lunenburg, and we could not get the work done in North Cape Breton and Ingonish. There are a few items that appertain to North Cape Breton and Victoria which it might have been very nice and convenient to have in the estimates last year, but which were not expended. Speaking as one of the members from that section, I hope the minister will find his way clear to see that the expenditures are made this year.

Item agreed to.
North West Cove (Tancook)

breakwater, wharf extension, $8,500.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Is this a new
work?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: It is an extension to an old work. The extension is required in order to provide adequate landing facilities at this point, also for the protection of 133 boats which fish from this place.

Item agreed to.
Port Greville-breakwater reconstruction, $40,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What is the present condition of this work?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is for reconstruction of the breakwater. In 1923-24, there was an appropriation of $24,000 and an expenditure made of $11,908. This breakwater was badly damaged by a storm and unusually heavy ice last year, which necessitated the rebuilding of practically the entire structure. Sixty feet of the shore-ward section was reconstructed during the year 192324. The breakwater protects the harbour, and without the breakwater it would very shortly become unnavigable.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The vote in
1923-24 was $24,000. The revote is $10,000, while the total vote now is $40,000. That [DOT]would look as if we had spent $14,000 last year.

Supply-Harbours and Rivers

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: We did not.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Then there is
ti larger revote than the figures show.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: When the Estimates were being made up, it was assumed that there would be an expenditure of $14,000, but the actual expenditure was $11,908.19.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
So that when
we are voting $40,000, it is not $40,000 in addition to $14,000 already spent?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: That is how it would appear on these estimates. I just point that out because it is misleading. What is the reason for the increase of $16,000?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Additional damage was done by the storm and unusually heavy ice last year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Was the work
that cost $11,908 injured?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: No.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the
name of the contractor?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The work was
done by day labour.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What is the explanation of having work done on a job of this size by day labour?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
We started to do this work by contract and we prepared to enter into a contract when this storm occurred.
I hat changed the whole situation as regards contracting, and there were many extras in addition. The department decided to make the expenditure themselves and a contract was not entered into. For this year we are asking for tenders for the completion of the work. Item agreed to.
Port Hood-wharf repairs, $5,800.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
We had this
matter up last year and all that was necessary was $8,600. That was spent. What has happened since?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
A contract was
entered into with the Sydney Construction Company for $7,796. In August a further contract for extension was entered into to provide a new block to be placed at a distance of 18 feet from the end of the old work. It is reported that this appears to be due to the falling in of material from the sides which prevented an even or level bearing for the block. [Sir Henry Drayton.J
As a result it was found necessary to construct a connecting block 29 feet in length. This work was authorized August 28, 1923, as an extra to the contract.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The original
contract was $7,400.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: It was $7,798.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It was within
the vote?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
While that
contract was being carried out, if I understand the minister correctly, an undisclosed condition developed and it was found necessary to make another contract. Why was it not dealt with by Governor General's warrant? Why is it brought in here?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: That has never been the practice.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
The act is
perfectly clear. I would again suggest that the minister should have a talk with the Auditor General. We have an Auditor General now and he might be used.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: We are coming before parliament and asking parliament to vote the amount now. The contract is being carried on at the present time. I am sure this is more satisfactory to parliament than issuing a Governor General's warrant.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: It is not satisfactory to parliament to have votes brought down that we cannot do anything with, when the minister says to us, "The money is all gone and it has to be paid".

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What would be the position in the case of a Governor General's warrant? It would be in the same position exactly.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Then there
would be a responsibility for it; and, in its turn, it has to be sanctioned by parliament and put in the proper place.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Exactly.	.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: This is an improper way of doing it. Has this money been paid?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: It cannot be paid until it is voted.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Of course not. The position is that when it is done in this way the matter is hung up.

Supply-Harbours and Rivers

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Parliament still
has control. If it were done by Governor General's warrant the money would have been paid.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: How idle to say that parliament still has control! Parliament is supposed to have some sense of decency. It is nonsense to say that parliament has control, and the hon. minister knows that it is nonsense. Any self-respecting parliament would not want a contractor to lose the money. Is the government going to make a practice of this?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I think my hon.
friend is hardly fair when he says it is not the proper practice. As a matter of fact it is the proper practice and this practice has been followed for many years. My hon. friend says that when it was found necessary to have an extension of the contract we should have obtained a Governor General's warrant. I do not think that procedure would be endorsed by this House. I think we have adopted the proper method. We asked for a certain amount last year and let the contract. During the contract certain conditions developed that required the letting of further work in order that the job might be properly done. That has been done and we come to parliament with this explanation asking for a vote. I quite disagree with my hon. friend when he says that has not been the practice. It has been the practice for many years.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I never said it
had not been the practice. I still say that it is an improper practice. The government does not like signing Governor General's warrants. It is a check on the extravagance of governments. It is supposed to be the only way in which no regard could be paid to the vote of parliament. It is supposed that money can only be paid out of the treasury when it is sanctioned by vote of parliament. Apparently the practice is to depart from that supposition. That is one of the reasons why I always advocated a pre-audit system. If you depart from the pre-audit system there is no check on the department and there is no help for the treasury; but I realize that it is no good talking to my hon. friend, and the Acting Minister of Finance (Mr. Robb) is not here.

Item agreed to.
Port Lome-'breakwater extension, $8,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What is this for?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
To construct a
cribwork extension 50 feet long by 40 feet
wide and 32 feet high to existing breakwater. This work is under contract with the Reid Construction Company of Granville Ferry, N.S. Owing to the lateness of the season when the contract was let it is not expected that any work will be done during 1923-24. The vote last year was $9,600 and this year $8,000. Tenders were received, the lowest tender being $7,168. This would be the amount required for completion.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What was the expenditure last year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: How could we * have spent that large amount last year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
We did not spend
it all last year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Will $8,000 complete everything?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Yes, that will
complete the work.

Item agreed to.
Port Medway-to purchase and extend wharf, $6,100.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
How much of a wharf
could be built for that sum? Is this wharf in Lunenburg county?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: No, in Shelburne and Queens.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Will the minister explain just what the wharf is needed for, who owns it, when the suggestion for purchase came, and how far the negotiations proceeded.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: There was a petition signed by some sixty-three residents calling attention to the public wharf at Port Medway, especially on behalf of the merchants and fishermen. They complained that they had not a wharf or a dock to lay a vessel to. The Minister of Finance (Mr. Fielding) visited this district in 1923, and he confirmed the statements as set out by the petitioners. During the storm of January 4, 1923, the old wharf was completely wrecked. There are certain industries located at this point. The Nova Scotia Wood, Pulp and Paper Company have mills at Charleston on Medway river, seven miles west from Port Medway. Their yearly output is 5,000 tons valued at $40 per ton.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Is that the wharf used
by the McLeod, McCurdy combination?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I do not know.
There is a letter here stating that a public

Supply-Harbours and Rivers
wharf is urgently required at this point. There is no place where the packet ship from Halifax may discharge her cargo, and there is enough business to be carried on at this point to justify the construction of a wharf.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
How far has the minister
got with the negotiations for the purchase of this wharf from private interests?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
No purchase has
been made yet. There is an estimate by the department that the site will cost $2,500.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is that to be expropriated?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: It will depend on whether the owner agrees to a price which the department considers fair and reasonable.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Who is the owner?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: J. N. Wilde.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
How big will the wharf
be?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
It will be 225
feet long by 25 to 90 feet wide. The extension will be pile work 40 feet long by 90 feet wide.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: How many other wharfs are there at this point?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The pulp company have a wharf near there.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is there a wharf on this site at the present time?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
There is an old
wharf.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Are there any
others?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Not to my knowledge.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What is (he size of the other wharf that is mentioned?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I have no information regarding the pulp wharf.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What are the
complaints against the man who runs this wharf? Why is it thought better to have the government purchase the wharf?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The present wharf is not being maintained, and to-day the public are without any accommodation at all.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is not the other wharf which you are buying available for the general public?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: It was, but it is not being maintained by Mr. Wilde, and today it is not safe for use.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What is the
record of the business done over it?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: We have no information.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Does the minister know if Wilde made any dock charges or not?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I have no information. During the storm last year a steamer was lying at this wharf, which became more or less wrecked, endangering the steamer and causing considerable expense and delay.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
What was the
date of Mr. Fielding's visit?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: His letter submitting the petition of the residents is dated February, 1923. In May and October of the same year he wrote strongly urging the necessity of wharfage accommodation.

Item agreed to.
Shelburne-wharf repairs, $1,500.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What is the necessity for the extra grant there when we already have the contract of last year?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: We are renewing the guard timbers and placing new mooring posts and rings.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What did we spend $5,000 for the year before?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
In 1923-1924 there
was a renewal of the top at an expenditure of $4,478.39. This is to complete the work.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Was that by
tender?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: No, by day labour.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I do not suppose the minister misled the House last year when he said that the work would be done for $4,500. The estimate proved $1,500 too low?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Quite right.

Item agreed to.
Ship Harbour-wharf, $4,100.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
This is new
work?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
There was an estimate for this work last year, for "wharf repairs at Ship Harbour." The word "repairs" was inserted in error, as the appropriation was clearly for the construction of a wharf as explained by the minister at page 4586 of Hansard. The minister then said:
Ship Harbour is in Halifax county. The estimated cost is the amount oi the vote. It is to construct

Supply-Harbours and Rivers
a pilework wharf 80 feet long and 20 feet wide with an ell 20 feet by 30 feet. The purpose is to provide shipping accommodation for the residents of Ship Harbour and the surrounding districts by shortening the haul from the mills to the now only available wharf by a distance of about 41 miles, over a very hilly road. It is a fanning and fishing district.
Last year there was an error in setting out the vote in the estimates. It is construction, not repair, so we are asking for the vote this year. The work was not done last year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: What representations have been made asking for this work?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: That information is given in the explanation which I just read.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I have had an opportunity of visiting that section of country and it is one of the finest harbours in the world. The people there have no facilities for carrying on their business. If the hon. member could only come down to Nova Scotia I would be glad to arrange to take him on an automobile drive of ninety or a hundred miles in Hants county which would show him the beauty of that part of the country.

Item agreed to.
Tiverton-breakwater extension, $14,000.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I see this is a revote.
Are most of these revotes due to the fact that supply was voted too late last year to get the work done?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Largely, yes.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: In view of the statement made by the minister a short time ago I suggest that the House should meet earlier in the season. There are several reasons for that. One is, as the minister has said, that supply is voted so late that it is impossible to carry on this worjk, and it is just possible that the construction of a good deal of this new work from year to year has been due to the fact that work began too late in the fall owing to the late voting of supply. Then there is another important reason: A great many hon. members would rather be in session here during the winter than during the summer. I urge strongly upon the government that the estimates be brought down earlier in the session and that the session be called earlier in the year.

Item agreed to.
Walton-breakwater repairs, $1,800.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I would ask a question generally about these breakwaters. I understand 244
there is a deep tide there, and I wondered what height above the natural water these breakwaters were.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Before the minister answers I may say to my hon. friend that he is speaking on the item relating to Walton, which is in the county of Hants. Walton is the home of my ablest opponent in the last election, Mr. Parsons. I have nothing against him personally. He and I are close personal friends, though we do not step with the same foot politically. If $15,000 or $20,000 was being voted for this purpose I would support it, because as a matter of fact I asked for 150 per cent more than what is provided in these votes for ordinary repairs. In all the districts where these votes are given the majority of the people are neither Liberal nor Progressive, but Conservative; nevertheless when it comes to a question of the encouragement of industry I believe in taking the necessary steps irrespective of what people carry on that industry or what their political beliefs are. The hon. member (Mr. Gould) probably does not know our section of the country. I would like him to come down there some time and see it, not in the spring when those fogs prevail which are the bane of the people of our province, but when the apple trees are in blossom, when gypsum quarries, of which Mr. Parsons is a great operator, are working, and when the lumbermen are shipping their products. The tides in that section of the country from time to time recede to such an extent as to leave the rivers nothing but beds of mud.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Is the hon. member in order? We wrant to get on with the business. We do not want to be here forever.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: The hon. member (Mr. Gould) referred to the height of the wharf above the tides. If my hon. friend (Mr. Lewis) is a landlubber he had better be patient. If hon. members would come down to my part of the country they would be in a position to criticise, adversely or otherwise-

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
We are trying to pass
the item.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
No, you are trying to
obstruct it.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: I merely rose to ask for information, and the question is not yet answered.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
I understood that the hon. member (Mr. Martell), who has knowledge of the locality, had given the information. The height of the wharf is 24 feet; that would be from the bottom sill up. I do



Supply-Harbours and Rivers
not know the extent of the tides there, but I suppose the top would be four or five feet above high water.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext: Have the engineers taken into consideration the pressure of the tides and have they made an estimate of what the total cost would be to complete the work so as to make it permanent in its character at these various points and render unnecessary these haphazard votes year in and year out?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
They are not
haphazard; the works are all carefully gone into by the engineer in charge. Many of these works are timber and stone cribwork which are subject to decay and deterioration. There will be annual repairs. My hon. friend, I think, has in mind the hope of permanent construction, something that will wipe out these annual votes. Permanent construction on our coast line, with the present population, would be a very formidable task to undertake. We find that in view of the character of the works and the service they are supposed to render the manner in which we are carrying on these works is the most economical one.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
If my hon. friend from
Assiniboia would come down there he would find it is absolutely impossible, unless you spend millions and millions of dollars, to make a permanent structure along the Avon river and in Minas Basin. We have there the highest tides in the world, and you may dredge around the wharves to make berths for the vessels, but in the winter season the water freezes and afterwards you have these immense tides that carry the mud right back again, so it is practically a continuous task to keep these harbours clear.
Mr, CALDWELL: How high is the tide, thirty-six feet?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OP PUBLIC WORKS-HARBOURS AND RIVERS-NOVA SCOTIA
speechtext:
Up to sixty feet. My
hon. friend has evidently not been over that portion of the country, but as usual he is a sailor, a marine engineer, a dredger, and a lawyer too.

Item agreed to.
Progress reported.

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE

speechtext: Mr. MACKENZIE KING moved the adjournment of the House.

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE
speechtext:
May I ask if the House
is sitting to-morrow? It is Dominion Day, and I think we ought to recognize that as a holiday.
[Mr. J. H. Kina.J

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE
speechtext:
I announced
in the House a few days ago that it was the intention to sit on Dominion Day, and no objection was taken. I doubt if there is any better way in which we could observe the holiday.

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE
speechtext: Then why not observe them all that way? I do not see why we should disregard our country's birthday, our own particular holiday.

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE
speechtext:
I think myself it is a
mistake for us to be sitting on Dominion Day. The Prime Minister did mention it on Friday, immediately after the opening of the House. I did not catch it myself, or I would have objected then. Dominion Day is perhaps the most outstanding holiday of the year, the commemoration of the birth of this country. We are, I know, pressing to get through the work of the session at this period, but it seems too bad to be observing every manner of holiday as a holiday all through the session, and then to ignore altogether the one that really means more to our country than perhaps any other.

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE
speechtext:
I submit we
are not ignoring the holiday in attending to the country's business. In Great Britain the House of Commons sees fit to sit on the King's birthday and on other days that are set apart as holidays. I am inclined to think the country wull back up our position very strongly to attend to the country's business on the holiday.

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE
speechtext:
I would object less to
sitting on the 24th of May than to sitting on the anniversary of the birth of our own country. It seems to me it is overdoing it to be sitting then. If that is not ignoring the holiday, there is no other way of ignoring a holiday that I know of.

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE
speechtext:
When we were sitting
in the Museum in 1919 the session lasted, if my memory serves me right, until the 10th of July, and we sat on Dominion Day. I have sitting beside me the hon. member for Queens (Mr. Sinclair), now occupying the treasury benches, and he remembers very well that the House sat on that day, and the session was prolonged until the 10th of July. If that was right when my right hon. friend was leading the government, or when he was one of the real leaders of the government, I do not see why it should be wrong to-day.

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE
speechtext:
Do the civil servants get a
holiday to-morrow if the House sits? I think they ought to get the holiday.

Home Bank Investigation-Report

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: ADJOURNMENT-BUSINESS OF THE HOUSE
speechtext:
Although it does inconvenience a great many of us, particularly the members from the West, I do think we should observe the 1st of July. Of all days of the year I think it is the most important, and if Canada ever means anything to us I think parliament should set a standard in that regard.
Mr. MA.R,TELL:	I am absolutely in accord with the right hon. leader of the opposition and with the hon. members for Calgary. Surely if we have a birthday in this country we should observe it. We keep all manner of holidays in this country, as the leader of the opposition has said, and we sit night and morning to make up for them. For heaven's sake, let us have some pridte in our country and observe Dominion Day.
Motion agreed to and the House adjourned at 11.50 p.m.
Tuesday, July 1, 1924.
